newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-AKRAM DOUBTFUL FOR FIRST TEST IN SRI LANKA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AKRAM DOUBTFUL FOR FIRST TEST IN SRI LANKA.

text.p: Pakistan captain Wasim Akram is doubtful because of injury for the first of two tests against Sri Lanka starting on Saturday.
"My bowling arm is not 100 percent fit. The ligaments have got weak by playing too much cricket," Akram told Reuters in an interview on Tuesday.

All-rounder Akram, the only player in world cricket with more than 300 wickets in both test and one-day internationals, arrived with his team on Monday for a short tour including only one match outside of the tests.
"The injury became quite bad in (the recent) Sharjah (Cup) and I am under treatment now. The only cure is rest," said Akram.
"I can't bowl nor bat. I am taking my time to see if it improves, but my chances are quite remote."
The Pakistan skipper was a mere spectator at a cricket club here on Tuesday where he watched most of his squad practice.

Two of the party, Salim Malik and Ijaz Ahmed, along with coach Mushtaq Mohammad, have yet to arrive for the tour which opens on Wednesday with a two-day game against a Sri Lanka Board XI captained by Marvan Atapattu.
Atapattu, Sri Lanka's number three batsman who has virtually replaced Asanka Gurusinha, is one of the young players with whom Akram has been impressed.
"Sri Lanka were an improved side before the World Cup. I think they need some young blood," said Akram.
"They need a couple of young batsmen like Atapattu, who is a good player. Then they will be okay," he said.
Akram was confident his side would be successful in the two-test series.
"Sri Lanka played better than us in Sharjah and they deserved to win. But test cricket is an entirely different ball game altogether," said Akram.
"Bearing in mind we are playing in Sri Lanka, I am confident we will give them a good fight and I have full confidence we will do well."
